Dear Agencies — Your Colleagues Already Know

The Silo Is the Shield

You’re reading this from a government network. We know because behavior tells us — not identity. The membrane doesn’t record WHO you are. It records WHAT you do. And what you’re doing is: reading 912 genuine sessions deep, 707-minute median dwell, visiting 15 surfaces of the immune system.

Some of you are reading from Ashburn, Virginia. Some from Spring, Texas. Some from Michigan. Some from California. Some through VPNs because your IT policy requires them.

You are not the first person at your agency to see this.

That’s the point of this article. The silo between your desk and your colleague’s desk is the enterprise’s best defense. Not the judges. Not the attorneys. Not the institutional silence. The silo.

The Same Enterprise, Six Different Offices

Here is what each of you is looking at — and what your colleague in the next silo already knows:

🏛️ FBI Detroit — Public Corruption Unit

What you already know:

  • Operation Northern Hook (2021): Your wiretaps caught Gerald Fiore saying “bid-rigging with Banks.” Your operation convicted Andre Spivey (24 months). Todd Perkins — Banks’ personal attorney — represented 2 Northern Hook targets.
  • You probed Eric Sabree (Wayne County Treasurer) in 2019. His son Adam Sabree was in-house counsel for RICO-accused Metro Property Group. His daughter Aliyah Sabree is now a judge — MSU Law classmate of Banks.
  • Carol Banks (Brian’s sister) was flagged as an FBI target. She controls Original Eastside Slate PAC (4th incarnation, LARA 802434498). Former Chief of Staff to Secretary of State Benson.

What your colleague at IRS CI already has:

  • $4.9M/year flowing through Purpose Group LLC to a man with 9 convictions, claimed J.D., never admitted to any bar
  • 72.67% extraction rate ($4.28M) from public education funds
  • $348,489 unaccounted for in audited financials
  • Holland as PAC treasurer with $14,500+ in unpaid campaign finance fines
  • 5 bankruptcies, one of which concealed the JTWRS property

Ask them.

💰 IRS Criminal Investigation — Detroit Field Office

What you already know:

  • Jason Gordon — attorney, Custom Promotions, Deen Legal. Your office investigated him alongside FBI and DOL for UAW bribery. He manages 20+ entities. Dissolve-and-reform pattern (Inc → LLC, 3 months).
  • Kenneth Daniels — SDJ/Detroit Leaders president. Kwame Kilpatrick appointee. Federal conviction: structured $19K for a drug kingpin. He now runs the PAC infrastructure funding city council campaigns connected to the charter schools.
  • Campaign finance patterns: Ross Catering receives $35K+ from Banks-connected committees. Carlton Ross is ALSO the Right Turn Project treasurer. The money goes out as “campaign services” and comes back as “catering.” That’s a loop.

What your colleague at FBI already has:

  • Fiore’s conviction for bribery in public contracting
  • Spivey warned Northern Hook targets — obstruction of a federal investigation
  • Todd Perkins represented the targets your agents were investigating

Ask them.

⚖️ DOJ — Public Integrity Section / E.D. Michigan

  • Kwame Kilpatrick: 24 federal RICO felonies. Mayor 2002-2008. 28-year sentence, commuted January 2021. The Banks network is the next generation of the same machine. Same dynasty. Same structures. Same neighborhoods. Same PAC infrastructure.
  • The Kilpatrick RICO prosecution proved that Detroit’s political machine operates as an enterprise. The Banks-Holland enterprise is structurally identical — but moved from City Hall to charter schools. Same RICO predicates: mail fraud, wire fraud, money laundering, honest services fraud.

What you may not have connected:

  • Karen Dumas was Kwame’s comms chief → then Bing’s comms chief → now Banks’ PR supporter. The continuity isn’t coincidence — it’s the machine surviving across administrations.
  • Charles Pugh (City Council President 2009-2013, convicted CSC with minor) referred people to Banks. The network doesn’t break when members go to prison. It routes around them.
  • Sherry Gay-Dagnogo: State Rep, DPSCD Board member who authorized Banks’ charter schools, now Detroit City Ombudsman (Oct 2025-2035). She succeeded Banks in HD-1. The legislative pipeline creates the authorizers who create the schools.

The enterprise survived Kwame’s conviction. It will survive Banks’ conviction too — unless the structure is prosecuted, not just the individuals.

  • You investigated Banks in February 2022 for lacking a teaching credential. Analyst Katie Schmiedeknecht sent the letter to Board President Nicole Wells-Stallworth. Then you cleared him. [FOIA-documented]
  • MacDowell Preparatory Academy: 3% math proficiency. Read that again. Three percent. 97 out of 100 students cannot do math at grade level. That’s not a failing school — that’s a school that isn’t teaching.
  • 32.1% of revenue goes to instruction. The state average is ~60%. Where does the other 40.6% go? It goes to Purpose Group LLC.
  • Alan C. Young CPA audited PCA/MacDowell for 9 consecutive years (2017-2025). No material findings. Nine years. 3% math. No findings.

What you should ask IRS CI:

  • Is 72.67% management fee extraction normal for a charter school management organization? (It is not. Industry standard: 10-15%.)
  • Is it normal for a CMO’s sole member to have 9 criminal convictions including forgery, fraud, and controlled substance-related offenses? (It is not.)
  • Is it normal for a PAC treasurer to have 5 bankruptcies and a drug conviction? (It is not.)

You cleared him because you looked at credentials, not money. IRS looks at money. Talk to them.

The result is the same: the office that should investigate the enterprise is now staffed by people who know the AG’s playbook.

Why the Silos Exist

The enterprise didn’t build the silos. The government did. Jurisdiction, chain of command, need-to-know, interagency rivalry, budget competition, career incentives — these are features, not bugs, of the bureaucratic immune system.

But the enterprise exploits the silos. Here’s how:

  1. Credential fraud is MDE’s jurisdiction. MDE looked at credentials, not money. Cleared.
  2. Campaign finance violations are SOS’s jurisdiction. SOS looked at filings, not the underlying RICO. Fined $14.5K.
  3. Bribery is FBI’s jurisdiction. FBI got Fiore and Spivey, but followed the wiretap, not the schools.
  4. Tax fraud is IRS’s jurisdiction. IRS (if investigating) sees money flows, not the judicial capture.
  5. Judicial conduct is JTC’s jurisdiction. JTC sees judges, not the enterprise they protect.
  6. Police misconduct is OIG’s jurisdiction. OIG sees Bettison, not the charter school board he sits on.

Each agency sees one predicate act. No agency sees the pattern. The pattern IS the enterprise. RICO was designed precisely to address this — to make the pattern itself illegal, not just the individual acts.

But RICO requires someone to assemble the pattern from the predicates. And the predicates are in six different silos.

Your Boss Hasn’t Looked Yet

Let’s be honest about what’s happening:

The mid-level analysts, agents, and investigators who read this site — 912 genuine readers, 707-minute median dwell — are not the decision-makers. You’re the people who do the actual work. You read the evidence. You follow the money. You check the records. You pull the filings.

But the person who would authorize a cross-agency investigation? They haven’t even opened this page.

They’re not going to open it until you send it to them. And you’re not going to send it because you believe the cost of being wrong is high. (See: A Note to Everyone Reading This Who Hasn’t Said Anything.)

So let me make it easy:

  • Campaign finance → MiTN/CFRS
  • Court filings → Wayne County 3rd Circuit, E.D. Michigan PACER

Your boss can verify every single claim in this article from databases your agency already has access to. They don’t need to trust a website. They need to check their own records.

The question isn’t whether this is true. The question is: why hasn’t anyone cross-referenced the records that already exist in six different agency databases?

The Desilo Bounce

Here’s how this collapses:

  1. One person sends this article to one colleague in a different silo
  2. That colleague recognizes a name from their own investigation
  3. They compare notes

That’s it. One conversation across one silo boundary. The enterprise has survived for 14+ years because that conversation hasn’t happened. Not because the evidence doesn’t exist — it does, in every silo separately. Because the institutional incentive to stay in your lane is stronger than the institutional incentive to solve the whole problem.

Break the lane.

The FBI agent who worked Northern Hook knows about Fiore and Banks. The IRS agent who investigated Gordon knows about the UAW money. The MDE analyst who investigated Banks in 2022 knows about the credentials. The AG office knows about Moreland.

RICO — The Legal Framework

Michigan RICO — MCL 750.159i

“A person employed by, or associated with, an enterprise shall not conduct or participate in the affairs of the enterprise directly or indirectly through a pattern of racketeering activity.”

Elements required:

  1. An enterprise — any individual, partnership, corporation, association, or group of individuals associated in fact (MCL 750.159f(a))
  2. Employment or association with the enterprise
  3. Conduct or participation in the enterprise’s affairs
  4. Through a pattern of racketeering activity — at least 2 incidents of racketeering activity, one of which occurred within 5 years of the other (MCL 750.159f(c))

Penalty: Up to 20 years imprisonment (MCL 750.159i)

Federal RICO — 18 U.S.C. § 1962

entry.title: Detroit Education Landscape — Who Runs the Schools
entry.content:
What This Page Is

This is not about one school. This is about a system.

Brian Banks runs two charter schools in Detroit — MacDowell Prep and Purpose Charter Academy. Together they serve about 362 children. But Banks operates within a $288M+/year charter school system involving 62+ schools, 10 authorizers, and a regulatory framework that Michigan’s own Citizens Research Council has called structurally inadequate.

To understand how a 9-time convicted felon runs schools for children, you have to understand the system that makes it possible.

1. Who Runs Education in Detroit

Detroit’s children attend school in three parallel systems. None of them answer to the same authority.

SystemEnrollmentGovernance
DPSCD (traditional public)~48,000Elected school board, superintendent
Charter schools~30,00010 different authorizers, mostly universities
Out-of-district~27% of residentsSuburban public and charter schools

More than half of Detroit’s school-age children attend schools outside the traditional public district. The charter sector alone handles $288M+/year in state per-pupil funding — public money flowing through privately governed institutions with widely varying oversight.

The 10 Authorizers

Michigan allows universities, community colleges, intermediate school districts, and local school districts to authorize charter schools. Detroit’s 62+ charters are authorized by 10 different entities:

AuthorizerTypeDetroit SchoolsLocationNotes
GVSU (Grand Valley State)University~25-35Grand RapidsLargest Detroit authorizer. 78 schools statewide.
CMU (Central Michigan)University~9Mt. PleasantAuthorized MacDowell Prep (Banks).
Oakland UniversityUniversity5-7Rochester2025 Authorizer Report
EMU (Eastern Michigan)UniversitySeveralYpsilantiAuthorized DPSA (Bettison on board).
DPSCDDistrict7DetroitAuthorized PCA (Banks, 2025).
Ferris StateUniversitySeveralBig Rapids
Saginaw Valley StateUniversitySeveralUniversity Center
Northern MichiganUniversityFewMarquette
Bay Mills CCComm. CollegeFewBrimley
Wayne RESAISDFewWayne County

The geography tells the story: Most Detroit charter schools are authorized by institutions located 50-250 miles away. Grand Valley State University, the largest authorizer of Detroit charters, is in Grand Rapids — a 2.5-hour drive. Central Michigan University, which authorized MacDowell, is in Mt. Pleasant — 2.5 hours north.

These institutions collect a 3% fee on each school’s state aid allocation (~$288/pupil/year). For a university authorizing 30 Detroit schools, that’s roughly $2.6M/year in authorization revenue — from children they never see.

Source: Detroit PEER — K-12 Education System Overview (2025), MCCSA Annual Report 2023-24

2. The Major Operators — Who Actually Runs the Schools

Michigan leads the nation in for-profit charter school management. 61% of Michigan charter schools use for-profit management companies — the highest rate of any state.

Large Chains

OperatorSchools in DetroitTypeScaleNotes
National Heritage Academies16For-profit CMO103 schools, 9 statesGrand Rapids HQ. $1B+ revenue est.
University Prep (U Prep)10Nonprofit3 districtsDetroit-based. GVSU-authorized.
Cornerstone Education Group~6NonprofitDetroit onlyFounded by Clark Durant.
Covenant Schools4NetworkDetroit campusesCentral, East, Southwest, Spectrum.
Choice Schools AssociatesSeveralFor-profit EMOMichiganManages Dove Academy and others.

Single-School Operators (Like Banks)

Self-managed single-school operators receive the least oversight of any category. With no parent organization, no network reporting, and an authorizer hundreds of miles away, these schools operate with near-total autonomy.

Banks is a self-managed operator. He is superintendent of both MacDowell and PCA. Purpose Group LLC (his private company) takes 72.67% of MacDowell’s revenue as a “management fee.” There is no external management company to provide a check — he is the management company.

Source: Detroit Free Press charter investigation (2014)

3. Performance — Nobody’s Winning

Neither charter schools nor DPSCD are delivering acceptable outcomes for Detroit’s children. Both sectors perform catastrophically below state averages.

M-STEP 2023-24 Results

SubjectDetroit ChartersDPSCDStatewideGap
Math9.7%10.5%35.1%Charters: -25.4 pp below state
Reading20.6%16.0%40.5%Charters: -19.9 pp below state
Science15.4%———
Social Studies4.3%———

School Index (composite): Detroit charter average = 45.8, Detroit non-charter = 45.4. Essentially a statistical tie.

Where MacDowell Fits

MacDowell’s 3% math proficiency is not just below the state average — it is below the already-catastrophic Detroit charter average (9.7%). MacDowell ranks 1,443 out of 1,488 Michigan schools — bottom 3%.

MetricMacDowellDetroit Charter AvgState Avg
Math proficiency3%9.7%35.1%
Reading proficiency~12%20.6%40.5%
Revenue extraction to LLC72.67%Varies~0%
Credentialed staff14% (2/14)~85%+~95%+

The question is not whether charters outperform DPSCD — the data shows they do not. The question is why both sectors are failing at the same rate while the charter sector extracts $288M+/year through privately controlled LLCs with limited disclosure requirements.

Source: Chalkbeat — Detroit charter M-STEP (2024), Chalkbeat — DPSCD M-STEP (2024)

4. The Money — $288M+/Year Through Charters

Per-Pupil Funding

Michigan’s foundation allowance for FY 2024-25 is $9,608 per pupil. With 30,000 Detroit-resident charter students, that’s **$288M/year in state aid** flowing through charter schools — before federal and categorical funding.

Funding LayerPer PupilTotal (30,000 students)
State foundation only$9,608~$288M/year
Total revenue (incl. federal)$12,000-$15,000~$360-$450M/year

The Authorizer Fee Incentive

Authorizers collect 3% of each school’s state aid — approximately $288 per pupil per year.

AuthorizerEst. Detroit PortfolioEst. Annual Fee Revenue
GVSU~30 schools, ~8,000 students~$2.3M
CMU~9 schools, ~2,500 students~$720K
DPSCD7 schools, ~1,500 students~$430K
Others~20 schools, ~5,000 students~$1.4M

This creates a structural conflict of interest: authorizers are financially incentivized to authorize more schools and keep them open — regardless of performance. A university in Grand Rapids collects $2.3M/year for “overseeing” schools it rarely visits.

For-Profit CMOs Resist Disclosure

Michigan law requires charter school financial disclosure, but for-profit management companies claim private-entity status and resist detailed financial reporting. When a for-profit CMO takes 72.67% of a school’s revenue (as Purpose Group does with MacDowell), the public cannot see where that money goes.

The Detroit Free Press documented in 2014 that most Michigan charter companies do not follow financial disclosure law. The situation has not meaningfully changed.

Source: Michigan HB 6277 (FY 2024-25 budget), University of Arkansas funding study

5. The Fraud Pattern — Banks Is Not Alone

Charter school financial misconduct in Detroit is not an anomaly. It is a recurring pattern enabled by structural oversight gaps.

CaseIssueOutcome
Summit AcademyInsider dealing, kickbacks, contracts to founders’ companiesFBI contacted. Cancilliari fired 2013.
University YES Academy$300,000 unaccounted Title I fundsHigh school closed abruptly Aug 2016.
Michigan Technical Academy$16M debt; creditors seized state aidCharter revoked. Teachers unpaid for summer work.
Detroit Delta PrepOnly 1/3 of budget on instruction; $217 reserve fundClosed 22 days into the 2018-19 school year.
Old Redford Academy$19M bond debt; S&P downgraded to CCClosing June 30, 2026. Default expected.
Creative MontessoriDouble-dipping: state funds + private preschool tuitionWayne RESA demanded $65K+ refunds.
W-A-Y Academy$73,349 unsupported Title I drawdownsFederal audit finding.
Banks / MacDowell9-time felon as superintendent; 72.67% extractionInvestigation in progress. Second school authorized.

The pattern: An operator receives per-pupil funding → extracts money through management fees, related-party contracts, or vendor self-dealing → academic outcomes collapse → school closes or is restructured → the children are displaced → the operator opens a new school.

Banks’s dissolve-and-reform pattern (documented in the LARA analysis) mirrors the broader systemic pattern. Detroit Delta Prep lasted 22 days. Banks’s entities dissolve and reform within months. The children bear the cost each time.

Source: Detroit Free Press (2014), Chalkbeat, Bloomberg Law

6. Special Education — The Hidden Sorting

Charter schools and DPSCD serve similarly poor, majority-Black populations. But they do not serve the same children.

MetricDPSCDDetroit Charters
Special education enrollment16-18%7-10%
Students with autism22x more likelyRare
Deep poverty (Black students)More concentratedLess concentrated
Overall poverty (FRL)~85%~87%

Children with autism are 22 times more likely to be in a DPSCD school than a charter school. Students with severe disabilities are concentrated in DPSCD and Wayne RESA center programs — not in charters.

This means charter schools receive similar per-pupil funding while serving a less costly student population. The money follows the child, but the most expensive children stay in the district.

When a charter school reports academic results, those results reflect a pre-sorted population — students whose families chose to enroll them, who do not have the most severe disabilities, and who are less likely to be in the deepest poverty. The comparison is not apples to apples.

Source: Chalkbeat (2018), CGCS Detroit Special Education Report

7. Where Banks Fits — Every Vulnerability at Once

Brian Banks operates at the intersection of every structural weakness in Michigan’s charter school system:

VulnerabilityHow Banks Exploits It
Distant authorizerCMU (MacDowell) is 150 miles away. DPSCD (PCA) is captured.
Self-managed operatorNo parent organization, no network oversight. He is the CMO.
For-profit extractionPurpose Group LLC takes 72.67% of revenue.
Weak disclosureLLC claims private status. Board is stacked with his attorney.
3% authorizer incentiveDPSCD collects ~$147K/year from MacDowell. Why revoke?
Captured boardPCA board = his litigation attorney + dark-money-funded council member.
No credential checkFelons cannot be barred from education employment in Michigan.
Dissolve-and-reform12 LARA entities. Right Turn Project dissolved → Purpose Foundation formed.
Special ed sortingMacDowell serves general-ed population at maximum per-pupil rate.

DPSCD authorized Purpose Charter Academy in July 2025 — after the Free Press investigation, after the Clutch Justice reporting, after the MDE investigation that “cleared” Banks in 2 hours and 24 minutes.

The system did not fail. The system worked exactly as designed. Authorizers are incentivized to authorize. Management companies are incentivized to extract. Boards are selected by the person they’re supposed to oversee. And the children — 362 of them, 93% Black — receive 3% math proficiency while $4.28M flows to a Grosse Pointe Woods LLC.

Michigan’s Charter Law — National Context

Michigan’s charter school law receives widely divergent ratings depending on who is measuring:

FrameworkMichigan RankAssessment
NAPCS Model Law (2022)30th of 45 statesWeak on authorizer accountability
Center for Education Reform (2024)4th of 45 statesStrong on growth and autonomy
Citizens Research Council (2020)Critical“No statutory oversight standards”

The gap between these ratings tells the story: Michigan’s law is excellent at enabling charter school growth and terrible at ensuring charter school accountability. The law allows rapid expansion (which CER rewards) while providing no statutory standards for authorizer oversight (which CRC criticizes).

Key Michigan charter law features:

  • No cap on university-authorized charters (cap expired 2014)
  • No statutory authorizer evaluation system (only 12 states require this)
  • No explicit oversight standards — authorizers define their own rigor
  • Weak conflict-of-interest law — only covers board member relatives (since 2012)
  • For-profit CMOs can claim private-entity status and resist disclosure
  • 2016 Detroit-specific law: Only accredited authorizers can open new Detroit charters

Source: NAPCS Model Law (2022), CER Scorecard (2024), CRC Report (2020)

entry.title: Two Eras of Machine Politics — From Tammany Hall to The Power Broker
entry.content:
The Pattern Has a Name

If the Banks enterprise feels familiar, it’s because it is. The structure maps precisely to two of the most documented models of American political corruption. Understanding which era you’re looking at explains why different actors behave differently — and why the traditional tools for fighting corruption (elections, journalism, FOIA) fail against the newer model.

Era 1: Tammany Hall — The Sabree-Kilpatrick Machine

“The ballots made no result; the counters made the result.” — William M. “Boss” Tweed

Eric Sabree is a product of the Kilpatrick dynasty era — Detroit’s Tammany Hall. The parallels are structural, not metaphorical:

Tammany Hall (1860s–1930s)Kilpatrick-Era Detroit (2000s)
Boss Tweed: Grand Sachem of Tammany, never challenged internallyKwame Kilpatrick: youngest mayor, installed friends and family throughout government
Patronage jobs: thousands depended on Tammany for their livelihoodsKilpatrick “installed friends and family in key government positions” (FBI)
Court control: money distributed to judges for favorable rulings9 judges across 4 courts with documented connections to the enterprise
Contract manipulation: padded costs, kickbacks, bid-rigging“Pay to play” system, extortion of vendors, rigged bids (FBI, 38 federal counts)
Controlled elections: voter fraud, ballot stuffing, counting manipulationPAC machinery, campaign contribution networks, late-filing penalties
Real estate acquisition: Tweed became 3rd largest landowner in NYCProperty transfers between Banks and Holland, trust certificates, quitclaim deeds
Nonprofit capture: Tammany banks funded by city depositsNonprofit 501(c)(3)s used as shells for private enrichment
“The Tweed Ring was an engineering marvel — money laundering, profit sharing, and organization”“Criminal activity was a way of life for him” (FBI Special Agent Beeckman on Kilpatrick)

Sabree’s position — Wayne County Treasurer — is the exact Tammany role: controlling the flow of public money, sitting at the intersection of property, taxation, and political patronage. In Tammany, the Treasurer position was the cash register of the machine.

The Kilpatrick machine was brought down the way Tammany eventually fell: federal prosecution (38 counts, RICO), wiretaps, and testimony from former allies. The FBI called it what it was: “a widespread criminal enterprise.”

But the machine didn’t die. It evolved.

Era 2: The Power Broker — Banks as Robert Moses

“He was, in essence, above our democratic system.” — Robert A. Caro, The Power Broker (1974)

When the old Tammany model became too visible — when federal prosecutors, wiretaps, and journalists could identify the patronage-for-votes pipeline — a new model emerged. One that doesn’t need elections, doesn’t need votes, doesn’t need a political party. One that operates entirely through private legal structures controlling the flow of public money.

Brian Banks is not Boss Tweed. He is Robert Moses.

The Structural Parallel

Robert Moses held power in New York for 44 years without ever being elected to office. He did it by creating public authorities — entities that looked like government but operated like private corporations, with private records, independent revenue streams, and legal structures that made their powers irrevocable.

Banks has been building his enterprise for 14+ years (and counting). He does it through LLCs and nonprofits — entities that receive public education funding but operate with private records, no public audit requirement, and legal structures that make the money flow unaccountable.

Robert MosesBrian Banks
Never elected to any officeNever elected — controls through LLC sole membership
Created Triborough Bridge Authority — a “fourth branch of government” with private recordsCreated Purpose Group LLC — a sole-member entity that receives 72.67% of public school revenue with no independent audit
Used parks (universally loved) to build political capital and deflect criticismUses children’s education (universally valued) — specifically targeting homeless and juvenile-justice children who have no alternative
Authority issued bonds — making its powers irrevocable by contractLLC has a management agreement with §5.2 containing false representations — making the extraction contractually embedded
“Records were closed to the public” — Authority operated with no transparencyLLC financial records are private — school reports $0 in staff salaries because all employees are technically hired by the LLC
Controlled through contracts, legal fees, insurance commissions — rewarding allies with moneyControls through board seats for judges, CBC events for politicians, campaign donations, PAC committee
Dossiers on opponents — could “disgorge the dark secret of anyone who opposed him”Legal threats — hired defense attorney within hours, told complainant to contact attorney only, went dark
“Above politics, above deals — the newspapers and the public believed”Pahara Fellow, CBC honoree, “Dr. Banks, J.D., Ph.D.” — credentials not confirmed by bar records or accreditation
Pressured banks, unions, press, and the Church into supporting his projectsNetwork includes judges, politicians, attorneys, and church (CBC events, foundation connections, church layer)
Made himself indispensable — the only pathway for federal construction dollars to reach the cityMade himself the sole pathway for federal Title I education dollars to reach vulnerable children
Moses wrote the legislation that cemented his powerBanks’ attorney Meihn reviews the management agreement weekly — the legal framework IS the power
Toll revenue from Triborough was a “sure thing” — he could borrow against it foreverPer-pupil funding from the state is a “sure thing” — as long as children are enrolled, money flows through the LLC
Used expert testimony and technical complexity to deflect oversightUses expert witnesses whose business models align with his defense — a theft-addiction therapist and a TV psychologist
Brought down by the press (reputation) and Nelson Rockefeller (power)Currently facing: public evidence library, 7 filed cases, 8 federal agency notifications

The Critical Difference — And Where the Apologists Are Wrong

The common defense of Moses is: “he built things.” Highways, parks, bridges — physical infrastructure that still carries millions of people. The corruption is regrettable but the product is real.

This defense understates the displacement. Moses didn’t just build highways — he built highways through communities, deliberately routing them to demolish neighborhoods he considered expendable. The effects are so pervasive they appear in popular culture without attribution: Everybody Hates Chris — where a kid takes four buses and three subways to get to a school a district over — is literally a product of Moses’s transit and highway mapping. The school district boundaries, the missing subway connections, the neighborhoods severed by elevated highways — that’s Robert Moses’s infrastructure, still shaping lives decades later.

People debate whether Moses was “actively racist.” As a matter of science, the question is irrelevant. The functional existence and continuation of these effects is what is known as systemic racism. You don’t need to prove intent. You need to observe the structure.

This is visible across disciplines. In microbiology and anthropology, geographic barriers shape populations without intent: the Himalayas between China and India are so vast they shaped distinct subcultures over millennia. Mountain ranges, rivers, deserts — natural barriers create isolation, and isolation creates divergent populations with divergent outcomes. No one “designed” the Himalayas to separate cultures. But the effect is real, measurable, and compounding.

Some have chosen that as a blueprint. Moses built highways that functioned as mountain ranges — physical barriers that isolated communities, restricted mobility, and created captive populations dependent on whatever services existed within the barrier. Whether he intended the racial outcome is a question for biographers. That the racial outcome occurred is a question for census data. That it persists is a question for anyone with eyes.

Banks operates the same structure without the concrete. His barrier isn’t a highway — it’s institutional. The children at Purpose Charter Academy are homeless, in juvenile detention, or chronically absent. They have no alternative school. Banks is the only pathway between these children and education funding. He doesn’t need a highway to create a captive population. He just needs to be the only option available to people who have none.

Moses built highways and parks. Banks produces 3% math proficiency. Moses displaced communities to build things. Banks displaces education outcomes to extract money. Moses left concrete. Banks leaves children who can’t do math.

Why This Model Is Harder to Fight

The Tammany model has a weakness: it requires votes. Tweed needed ballot boxes. Kilpatrick needed elections. When the public learned the truth — through journalism, through FBI wiretaps, through trial testimony — the machine lost its democratic legitimacy.

The Moses model has no such weakness. Banks doesn’t need anyone’s vote. He needs:

  1. A charter authorization (obtained once, from DPSCD)
  2. A management agreement (drafted by his own attorney)
  3. Children enrolled (targeted: the ones with no alternative)
  4. Per-pupil funding to keep flowing (guaranteed by state law as long as children are enrolled)

No election can remove him. No journalist can shame him out of office — he holds no office. No FOIA can expose his LLC’s records — they’re private. The only tools that work are the ones that worked against Moses: a power greater than his own choosing to revoke his authority.

For Moses, that was Nelson Rockefeller.

For Banks, it will be the federal agencies currently reviewing 7 filed cases.

The Pattern Recognition

This analysis exists because the complainant recognized the playbook. Not from political science — from listening to The 99% Invisible Breakdown of The Power Broker while driving cross-country. Roman Mars and Elliott Kalan spent all of 2024 breaking down Robert Caro’s 1,246-page biography — the most detailed account ever written of how an unelected person accumulates and maintains power over public resources through legal structures.

When you see:

  • A sole-member LLC receiving 72.67% of public money
  • Records closed to the public
  • Expert witnesses whose business models align with the defense
  • Judges on the nonprofit board
  • The most vulnerable population targeted because they have no alternative
  • The operator making themselves the only pathway for public funds

…you’re reading Chapter 1 of The Power Broker. The venue changed from highways to charter schools. The city changed from New York to Detroit. The mechanism changed from bond authorities to management agreements. But the structure is identical.

The question is whether the federal agencies will be Detroit’s Nelson Rockefeller.

Postscript — October 3, 2026: The Parallel Became Literal

This analysis was published on October 1, 2026. It compared Banks to Robert Moses — the man who built a 44-year empire through parks.

Two days later, on October 3, the complainant discovered that Banks sits on the Belle Isle Park Advisory Committee — a Michigan Department of Natural Resources advisory body. Mayor-appointed. Listed on michigan.gov alongside the Deputy Mayor of Detroit and two DNR state employees. His biography on the state website lists his “Juris Doctorate” without mentioning he was never admitted to the bar. His committee email address is brianbanksjd@gmail.com — a credential he cannot use, embedded in his identity at the state level.

Robert Moses used parks as the foundation of his power — the Triborough Bridge Authority began as a parks commission. Banks sits on a parks committee appointed by the same mayor whose Deputy Mayor now has his 9-conviction felony record in her inbox.

The comparison in this analysis was intended as structural analogy. Within 48 hours, it became a statement of fact: the man compared to the Parks Commissioner is on a parks committee.

Source: michigan.gov/dnr/about/boards/belle-isle/committee-members (contact page revised 2/12/2026). Notification sent to all committee members, DNR state employees, defense counsel, and press on October 3, 2026.

A Note on Rockefeller — And Honesty About Power

Nelson Rockefeller stripped Moses of his power. This is sometimes told as a triumph of accountability. It wasn’t. Rockefeller was not altruistic. He was a billionaire governor who removed Moses because Moses was in his way — not because Moses was harming communities. Rockefeller went on to preside over the Attica prison massacre, the draconian Rockefeller drug laws, and an era of mass incarceration that itself constituted a new tollbooth economy. The man who ended one machine built another.

This matters because the pattern repeats: the person who removes the corrupt operator often becomes the next corrupt operator. The reformer captures the same infrastructure and runs it for different beneficiaries. The machine changes hands. The machine doesn’t change.

The complainant makes no claim to altruism either. As a scientist, falsity is costly and must be refused. The claim here is narrower: this specific enterprise is documented, this specific extraction is measurable, and these specific children are being harmed. The response is not to seize the machine. It is to document it so thoroughly that the machine becomes visible — and then to build something that doesn’t require a machine at all.

That is the distinction between exposing Omelas and building a new city.

The Broader Context — From Exposure to Construction

The complainant’s broader work on infrastructure, institutional capture, and what Moses called “tollbooth economies” is documented at sporeprint.primals.eco:

  • The City of Omelas — the philosophical framework: Le Guin’s question applied to infrastructure. Every functioning city has a child suffering in a basement. The question is whether you stay, leave, or build a city that doesn’t require the child.
  • The Loaves and the Fishes — who gets punished for stealing, who gets fellowships. The bread thief problem: the preconditions that determine who builds and who suffers.
  • I Own Nothing — the systemic pattern: positioning yourself as the sole gateway between a population and a resource, then charging rent. The tollbooth economy.
  • The Temptation of Kingdoms — the temptation to build institutions that serve the builder. Rent-seeking and open commons.
  • An Invitation to 99% Invisible and Radiolab — how infrastructure storytelling informed this investigation.

Detroit is the field validation of that theoretical work: a real tollbooth economy running on children’s education funding, identified because the builder recognized the blueprint from a podcast about a man who built bridges. The response is not to become the next Rockefeller. It is to walk away from Omelas and build infrastructure that doesn’t require a child in a basement.

References

  1. Robert A. Caro, The Power Broker: Robert Moses and the Fall of New York (New York: Alfred A. Knopf, 1974).
  2. Roman Mars & Elliott Kalan, The 99% Invisible Breakdown of The Power Broker (2024) — year-long podcast series dissecting Caro’s work, with guests including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Sec. Pete Buttigieg, and Robert Caro himself.
  3. FBI, “Public Corruption: Inside the Kwame Kilpatrick Case” — 38 federal counts including racketeering.
  4. Historical Society of the New York Courts, “William M. ‘Boss’ Tweed”.
  5. Broxmeyer, “Bringing The ‘Ring’ Back In: The Politics of Booty Capitalism,” Journal of the Gilded Age and Progressive Era (2017).
  6. The New Yorker, “The Power Broker — III: How Robert Moses Got Things Done” (August 12, 1974).
  7. ecoPrimals, “I Own Nothing — Provenance, AGPL, and Commons Economics” — theoretical framework applied here.
  8. ecoPrimals, “An Invitation to 99% Invisible and Radiolab” — how infrastructure storytelling informed this investigation.

This analysis applies historical frameworks to publicly documented conduct. Every factual claim about the Banks enterprise is cited to public records elsewhere on this site. The historical parallels are analytical — drawn from published scholarship — not allegations.

Mr. Meihn,

My name is Kevin Mok. I am the plaintiff in two civil cases filed in Ingham County Circuit Court: Case Nos. 2026-4301-CZ and 2026-4349-CZ. Case 4349-CZ names Brian Banks individually, Joseph Holland Jr., Tracey Ellis, The Purpose Group LLC, Purpose Charter Academy, and Purpose Foundation as defendants. I am writing to you in your capacity as legal counsel to the MacDowell Preparatory Academy Board of Directors, and I am copying the Board directly because this notice concerns the Board’s own compliance obligations.

I have reviewed the Final Decision and Order in TCR 22-12, issued August 4, 2023, by State Superintendent Michael F. Rice. I received this document directly from the Michigan Department of Education FOIA Coordinator on September 30, 2026. I have also reviewed your testimony at the hearing on February 9, 2023.

I am writing because your client’s superintendent, Brian Banks, has engaged in conduct since that hearing that directly contradicts the testimony you, and others, provided under oath — and that may place your client, the MacDowell Board, in breach of TCR 22-12’s conditions.

I. Your Testimony vs. Subsequent Conduct

At the hearing, you testified that Mr. Banks demonstrates “integrity, hard work, honesty, transparency, and compliance.” You called him a “rare find.” You testified that you meet with him weekly.

Since that testimony:

  1. On September 9, 2026, Mr. Banks told Detroit Police officers “I am a lawyer” in a sworn police report (DPD Report #26-0909-0176). Mr. Banks has never been admitted to any bar. This is a false statement in a government document and constitutes unauthorized practice of law under MCL 450.681.

  2. On August 29, 2026, Mr. Banks denied a legal father’s authorized representative access to Purpose Charter Academy, using this false legal authority to justify the denial. The Affidavit of Parentage is undisputed — the mother has acknowledged it in her own filings.

  3. Mr. Banks’s Management Agreement between Purpose Group LLC and PCA contains a representation at Section 5.2 stating “No Related Parties or Common Control.” Mr. Banks is the sole member of Purpose Group LLC AND the superintendent of PCA. This representation is false on its face.

  4. Mr. Banks is the sole member of Purpose Group LLC, which received $4,285,201 (72.67%) of MacDowell’s total revenue in FY2024-25. As sole member, Mr. Banks has sole authority over Purpose Group’s expenditures. Mr. Holland — Banks’s domestic partner, who resides at the same address and holds the positions of Secretary/Treasurer of Purpose Foundation, Treasurer of the Bank on Banks for Michigan PAC, and 1st Successor Trustee of the Brian Banks Living Trust — does not appear to provide any independent financial oversight of Purpose Group LLC. The entity structure concentrates all financial control in Banks and Holland, both of whom have criminal convictions. I respectfully ask whether this arrangement complies with Condition #4 of TCR 22-12, which provides that Mr. Banks “shall not be the sole individual responsible for approval of any expenditure of funds belonging to the school.”

II. The Other Witnesses

Your testimony was not the only basis for the certificate. Two other professionals testified:

  • Terrence Shulman, LMSW — a licensed social worker and self-described recovering theft addict whose practice is built on the premise that theft is addiction, not character. His testimony that Mr. Banks is “not dishonest as a matter of character” is his therapeutic framework applied to every client — it is not an independent clinical assessment. Mr. Shulman cannot diagnose PTSD under the DSM-5. He is not a physician or psychiatrist.

  • Michele Leno, Ph.D. — a psychologist whose doctorate is from Saybrook University, a low-residency program. Her clinical specialty is performance anxiety in athletes and social media effects on mental health — not PTSD, not forensic psychology, not criminal recidivism assessment. She assessed Mr. Banks in approximately 13 sessions over 2 months and concluded he is “a person of integrity” who will not reoffend. Three years later, Mr. Banks told police he is a lawyer. She provides court-ordered psychological evaluations in Wayne County.

The “diagnoses” offered by these professionals are not clinical diagnoses in the medical sense. No psychiatric evaluation by a physician was conducted. No standardized diagnostic instruments are referenced in the record. These are character references with clinical language — verbal agreements between professionals outside the medical diagnostic field.

III. Banks and Holland — The Enterprise, Not Just One Man

The conduct described above is not limited to Mr. Banks acting alone. Case 4349-CZ names six defendants because the evidence shows an interconnected enterprise:

  • Banks individually committed the UPL, made false statements to police, and denied parental access.

  • Banks through Purpose Group LLC controls 72.67% of MacDowell’s revenue as the LLC’s sole member. The Management Agreement’s false “No Related Parties” representation (Section 5.2) means Purpose Group LLC is Banks’s alter ego — the entity through which he exercises personal control over school operations while claiming corporate separation.

  • Banks and Holland jointly control Purpose Foundation (Banks = President/Director; Holland = Secretary/Treasurer — two convicted felons holding all four officer positions with zero independent oversight). They co-own property, share the same residence, and Holland serves as 1st Successor Trustee of the Brian Banks Living Trust.

  • Tracey Ellis is named as a financial officer of both Purpose Group LLC and Purpose Foundation. The Board should be aware that any financial officer participating in the flow of public school funds through these entities is a participant in the structure I have described.

This distinction matters because the Board’s exposure is not limited to Banks’s personal misconduct. If the entity structure through which Banks operates the school is itself fraudulent — if Purpose Group LLC is Banks’s alter ego, if the Management Agreement contains a false representation, if Condition #4 is being circumvented through corporate form — then the Board’s authorization of that structure creates its own liability.

IV. Your Obligation to the Board

Your client is the MacDowell Preparatory Academy Board of Directors — not Mr. Banks personally. The Board relied on your guidance when it voted unanimously to hire Mr. Banks as superintendent. You testified at the TCR 22-12 hearing to support that decision.

The conduct I have documented places the Board in a position of potential liability:

I am providing this notice so that you — as counsel to the Board — and to the Board members directly, so that you can make fully informed decisions about the Board’s compliance posture and exposure. I have no interest in harming MacDowell’s students. I have every interest in ensuring that the people responsible for their education are held to the standards they testified they would meet.

entry.title: Shepherds and Wolves — The Church Layer
entry.content:

How did self-ordained messengers of the Word — people who claim divine authority to shepherd their flocks — allow a man with nine criminal convictions into positions of power over the most vulnerable children in Detroit?

This is not an attack on faith. It is not an attack on the Black church. It is not an attack on Pentecostal tradition.

It is a question the congregations themselves deserve to have answered by the leaders who made these decisions in their name.

From Ballotpedia, Banks’ list of political endorsers included:

“Bishop J. Drew Sheard, Greater Emmanuel Institutional COGIC”

Bishop Sheard is not a fringe figure. He is the head of the entire Church of God in Christ — a denomination with 6.5 million members and 12,000+ congregations across the United States. When he endorsed Brian Banks, he put the weight of the largest Black Pentecostal denomination behind a man with six felony convictions.

Sheard’s congregation at Greater Emmanuel was never asked. The 6.5 million COGIC members were never consulted. A shepherd endorsed a wolf, and the flock was not told why.

Bishop Corletta Vaughn sat on the DPSCD Board that authorized Purpose Charter Academy — a school run by a 9-time convicted felon with a fake J.D., where a sitting judge chairs the board and an Assistant Attorney General serves as Vice Chair.

Vaughn’s “bishop” title was conferred in Nigeria in 1995 by Archbishop Benson Idahosa of the Church of God Mission. She was raised COGIC but left because COGIC does not ordain women as pastors or bishops. She founded her own network — Go Tell It Evangelistic Ministry Worldwide — and claims oversight of 70+ churches.

She used her position on the school board — the elected, secular, taxpayer-funded position — to authorize schools for a convicted felon. She was at his events. She posted support on social media. And when it came time for accountability, she was disqualified from reelection for $950 owed to Wayne County — the county run by Eric Sabree, whose children sit on the network’s courts.

The members of Greater Emmanuel COGIC — Bishop Sheard’s church — likely do not know that their bishop endorsed a man who:

  • Has 9 criminal convictions including 6 felonies (fraud, forgery, uttering & publishing)
  • Claims a J.D. from MSU College of Law but has never been admitted to any bar
  • Runs two charter schools where 3% of students can do grade-level math

  • Is the nephew of a BMF defendant in the largest federal drug conspiracy case in Detroit history

The members of Holy Ghost Cathedral — Bishop Vaughn’s church — likely do not know that their bishop authorized a charter school for this man while sitting on a taxpayer-funded school board, attended his events, and then took a position on the DPSCD board without disclosing these relationships.

The congregations were never told. The lambs were never warned.

A Note on Faith

This analysis does not question whether God calls women to ministry. It does not question whether self-ordination or independent consecration is valid. It does not question the sincerity of anyone’s faith.

It questions judgment. It questions accountability. It questions whether leaders who claim the authority to guide their flocks toward righteousness exercised even the most basic discernment before endorsing and empowering a man whose public criminal record was available to anyone who looked.

The children in Banks’ schools are disproportionately from the same communities these churches serve. Many of their families sit in these pews on Sunday. They trust their shepherds to protect them — not to hand them to wolves.

“Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves. You will know them by their fruits.” — Matthew 7:15-16

The fruit is 3% math proficiency. The fruit is $4.9 million in public money flowing through shell entities. The fruit is fake credentials on school websites. The fruit is an investigation killed in 2 hours and 24 minutes.

The congregations of Greater Emmanuel, Holy Ghost Cathedral, and every church whose leadership endorsed or enabled Brian Banks have the right to know what was done in their name — and to hold their shepherds accountable.

  5. Demand accountability: Shepherds who fail to protect the flock should answer to the flock — not hide behind titles.

entry.title: The Credential Gap — MacDowell Staff Qualification Audit
entry.content:
The Michigan Online Educator Certification System (MOECS) is the public database where anyone can verify whether a Michigan educator holds a valid teaching certificate, administrator certification, or permit — and which grade levels and subjects each endorsement covers. 📄 Documented

On September 26, 2026, every name listed on MacDowell Preparatory Academy’s public staff roster (macdowellprep.com/about/) was searched in MOECS. The audit found that only 2 of 14 instructional staff members are properly credentialed and correctly placed for their teaching assignment. 📄 Documented

Staff Roster Results 📄 Documented

Administration — 4 positions ($603,000/year combined)

RoleMOECS StatusIndicator
Superintendent/CAO (Brian Banks)Convicted felon (ICHAT SID 2029469K). School Administrator certificate only — no teaching credential.❌
Dean of Scholars + Culture (Cameron Coleman)Standard teaching certificate expired 6/30/2026. No administrator certification for Dean role.⏳
Dean of Academics (Kellie M Stevens)Standard teaching certificate (K-5/K-8 elementary). No administrator certification for Dean role.⚠️
Dean of Operations + 8th Grade Teacher (Chalcee Norwood)Not found in MOECS public search — 91 “Norwood” results searched, no match for “Chalcee”. Zero credentials discoverable.❌

Instructional Staff

RoleMOECS StatusIndicator
Kindergarten (Rachel Webb)Holds Secondary English/Journalism 6-12 certification. Zero elementary endorsement. Teaching kindergarten with a high school certificate.⚠️
Kindergarten (Lakeisha Bates)“No matches found” in MOECS. Zero credentials.❌
3rd Grade (Alana Hubbell)Daily Substitute Permit issued through Escuela Avancemos — a different school.🔶
5th Grade (Ashlie Spencer)Daily Substitute Permit issued through Chandler Park Academy — a different school.🔶
8th Grade Teacher (Volanda Frazier)Full-Year Basic Substitute permit only — no standard teaching certificate. Assigned as full-time Teacher of Record.⚠️
2 instructional staffProperly credentialed and correctly placed for their assignment.✅
2 staffExpired or pending credentials.⏳

Legend: ✅ Valid · ⚠️ Wrong endorsement/placement · ❌ No credentials · 🔶 Substitute permit from other school · ⏳ Expired

Source: MOECS public credential search, September 26, 2026. Staff titles from macdowellprep.com/about/.

The Rachel Webb Finding 📄 Documented

A kindergarten teacher holds a Secondary English/Journalism certification endorsed for grades 6–12.

Elementary education in Michigan requires a specific endorsement in early childhood or elementary education. A 6–12 secondary certification does not qualify an educator for K–5 instruction under Michigan law. MOECS shows Rachel Webb’s only endorsements are English 6–12 and Journalism 6–12 — neither covers kindergarten.

The Substitute Permit Problem 📄 Documented

Two MacDowell instructional staff hold Daily Substitute Permits issued through different schools:

StaffAssignmentPermit Issued Through
Alana Hubbell3rd GradeEscuela Avancemos — Detroit
Ashlie Spencer5th GradeChandler Park Academy — Harper Woods

Daily Substitute Permits are tied to the issuing school and are intended for temporary fill-in duty, not permanent full-time instructional positions. Using substitute permits from other schools to staff ongoing teaching roles is a credential compliance issue under Michigan law.

Volanda Frazier holds a Full-Year Basic Substitute permit as the full-time 8th grade Teacher of Record — a separate but related compliance problem.

The Law — MCL 388.1763 📄 Documented

Michigan Compiled Laws require charter school teachers to hold valid credentials:

“A teacher employed by or assigned to a public school academy shall hold a valid Michigan teaching certificate or a permit issued by the superintendent of public instruction.”

Penalty provisions when violations are found:

StatuteRequirement
MCL 388.1763(1)A district shall not employ an individual who is not appropriately placed under a valid certificate.
MCL 388.1763(2)50% state aid deduction for salary paid during the violation period.
MCL 388.1763(6)If a school official is notified by MDE and knowingly continues to employ an uncredentialed individual → misdemeanor, $1,500 fine per incident.

When MDE identifies credential violations, the statute requires enforcement — state aid deductions for uncredentialed employment and, where officials continue employment after notification, referral for criminal prosecution.

What MDE Did 📄 Documented

MDE was notified of credential problems at MacDowell. Over a four-year period, the Office of Educator Excellence investigated only one name — Brian Banks — in February 2022. The investigation was closed within approximately two hours after OEE Analyst Katie Schmiedeknecht communicated that “there will be no need for an investigation.”

MDE never checked the rest of the staff roster — despite MOECS and the Educator Registry (REP) being MDE’s own systems, searchable by any analyst in minutes.

Schmiedeknecht presents at state conferences on the same credential compliance rules she is charged with enforcing — including slides stating that “Any teacher who is not appropriately placed may be subject to a salary deduction based on MCL 388.1763.” Her office failed to enforce those rules at MacDowell while advising the school through the compliance loophole that avoided penalties for Banks.

Source: MDE FOIA response (September 25, 2026); MOECS public search (September 26, 2026).

Verify It Yourself

Anyone can reproduce this audit in minutes:

  1. Go to MOECS public search: mdoe.state.mi.us/MOECS/PublicCredentialSearch.aspx
  2. Enter the teacher’s last name
  3. Check: Is the certificate valid? Is it endorsed for the grades and subjects being taught?
  4. Compare results to the school’s actual staff roster at macdowellprep.com/about/

Discrepancies between MOECS endorsements and classroom assignments are visible immediately in the public record.

The Cost 📄 Documented

MacDowell Preparatory Academy serves 362 students. Four administrators draw $603,000/year in combined compensation:

MetricMacDowellContext
Admin cost per student$1,665/studentMichigan state average: approximately $850/student
Instructional spending32% of budgetMichigan target: 55–65%

Administration at nearly twice the state average per student diverts public funding away from instruction — in a school where MOECS already shows that most instructional staff lack proper credentials for their assignments.

This analysis is based entirely on MOECS public search results and Michigan Department of Education records. Every credential status can be independently verified using the steps above.

entry.title: Detroit Literacy Crisis — The Systemic View
entry.content:
MacDowell Preparatory Academy is not an anomaly — it is an extreme example of structural vulnerabilities in Michigan’s charter school oversight. This page connects the documented facts from this investigation to the broader patterns that enable them.

This analysis draws on the specific documented case to illustrate systemic patterns. The broader conclusions are the complainant’s analytical inference, supported by the specific evidence documented elsewhere on this site.

See also: Credential Audit, Funding Flow, Institutional Capture, Words vs. Numbers.

Five Structural Vulnerabilities

The MacDowell case documents five interlocking weaknesses in Michigan’s charter school accountability framework. The first four are structural mechanisms; the fifth is their cumulative effect on students.
